nodes.description:
The variant causes skipping of exon 2 and fusion of exons 1 and 3, which on the protein level is predicted to give the truncated product p.(Glu58ValfsTer80). The canonical full-length cDNA amplicon is absent in patient fibroblasts and a shortened amplicon appears in its place, and CAML protein is reduced on immunoblotting.
The residual protein matters for how this disease is read. A complete mouse null is embryonically lethal, so the small amount of CAML that survives this splice variant is the most likely reason the disorder is compatible with life at all - this is a hypomorphic allele, not a demonstrated human null.

nodes.description:
The biochemical signature of the disease, and the reason it is classified as a CDG at all. Serum transferrin isoelectric focusing repeatedly showed a type 2 pattern; capillary zone electrophoresis showed reduced pentasialo and raised trisialo transferrin; MALDI-TOF of serum transferrin N-glycans showed a CDG-II pattern. In parallel, apolipoprotein C-III isoelectric focusing showed absent asialo and disialo forms with only a trace of monosialo apoC-III, which is the standard readout of a mucin-type O-glycosylation defect.
Both arms of the defect are undersialylation of otherwise normally built glycans, which is what distinguishes this from the CDG in which the glycan is not assembled.

nodes.description:
The glycosylation abnormality in this disease is specifically one of terminal sialic acid addition, not of glycan initiation or of core processing. In fibroblasts, peanut agglutinin - which binds the Gal-beta(1-3)-GalNAc core 1 O-glycan only while it is unsialylated - gives a strong signal that is barely detectable in controls, while Vicia villosa lectin, which reports on the GalNAc initiation step, is unchanged. Established fibroblast markers of N-glycan hypoglycosylation (LAMP1, LAMP2, ICAM-1) were normal.
Sialyltransferases act in the trans-Golgi, so a sialylation-restricted defect localises the lesion to the late Golgi.

nodes.description: BET1L (GS15) is itself a tail-anchored protein, and unlike STX5 it is not merely displaced: total cellular levels fall to 37% of control in patient fibroblasts and to 30% on CAMLG knockdown in HeLa cells. The distribution between membrane and cytosol is normal, which is consistent with the proposal that poorly inserted BET1L is degraded before it can join an STX5 SNARE complex. YKT6, a Golgi SNARE that does not depend on the TRC pathway for insertion, is unaffected in both level and distribution - the internal control that makes the BET1L result specific.

nodes.description:
With STX5 partly cytosolic and its preferred partner BET1L depleted, the Golgi SNARE complexes that drive intra-Golgi and ER-Golgi fusion cannot be assembled normally. The morphological consequence is mild and was detectable only in the knockdown model - GFP-tagged ST6GAL1 showed a more fragmented distribution after CAMLG silencing, while patient fibroblasts stained for GM130 or TGN46 showed no obvious abnormality, and COG complex subunits were normally distributed.
That asymmetry is why this node is provisional rather than established: the SNARE measurements are solid in patient cells, but the Golgi disorganisation they are supposed to produce was demonstrated in a cell line, not in the patient's own fibroblasts.

nodes.description:
Tail-anchored proteins carry a single hydrophobic transmembrane domain at their C-terminus and therefore cannot use co-translational targeting; they are inserted post-translationally by the TRC pathway. Many of the ER-targeted substrates of that pathway are SNARE proteins or SNARE interactors, which is what makes a membrane-insertion defect present as a glycosylation disorder.
The defect is selective rather than global. Emerin, VAMP7 and VAPB - all canonically TRC-dependent - were normally localised in the patient's fibroblasts, which the authors attribute to residual CAML or to redundancy with the SND pathway.

nodes.description:
The clinical phenotype of CAMLG-CDG is neurological, progressive, and unexplained. Nothing published traces a route from the tail-anchored protein insertion defect, or from the hyposialylation it produces, to the developmental arrest, epilepsy, spasticity and brain atrophy that the child has. This node exists so that the clinical features hang off a mechanistic statement rather than floating free of the pathograph, and it is marked hypothetical because that is what it is.
Two observations bound the speculation. The phenotype is shared almost feature for feature with GET4-CDG, a defect at a different point in the same pathway, which argues that it is a property of the pathway rather than of CAML specifically. And GET3-CDG, also in the same pathway, presents instead as fatal infantile cardiomyopathy, which argues that the tissue affected is not determined by the pathway alone.

Total STX5 protein is normal, so this is a localisation defect rather than a stability defect.
The authors put this forward as a consistent cellular marker of TRC pathway dysfunction, which is its practical value: it is the assay that identifies a TRC pathway defect in a fibroblast line.
